chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Wāsiṭī, from one of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Allah created us from ʿIlliyyīn, and He created our souls from above that, and He created the souls of our Shi'a from ʿIlliyyīn, and He created their bodies from below that. So because of that, there is kinship between us and them, and their hearts yearn toward us.

key_terms.أَجْسَادَهُمْ: their bodies; referring to the bodily creation of the Shi'a as distinct from their souls
key_terms.أَرْوَاحَ شِيعَتِنَا: the souls of our Shi'a; indicating a shared elevated origin
key_terms.أَرْوَاحَنَا: our souls; referring to the souls of the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْقَرَابَةُ: kinship or closeness between the Imams عليهم السلام and their Shi'a
key_terms.تَحِنُّ: yearn or incline with affection and longing
key_terms.عِلِّيِّينَ: the exalted high realm from which the Imams and the souls of their Shi'a are described as being created
key_terms.قُلُوبُهُمْ: their hearts; the inner faculty that inclines toward the Imams عليهم السلام

ai.seo_question: Why do the hearts of the Shi'a incline toward the Imams عليهم السلام according to al-Kāfī?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a lofty mode of creation for the Imams عليهم السلام and explains the special affinity between them and their Shi'a. It presents that bond as rooted in origin, with the hearts of their followers naturally inclining toward them.
